points.response: Being inside 200 m is a data-layer matching parameter, not proof of being at the pick-up point; the driver's own recorded position during the whole wait was 181 m from the pin (F3) and the timeline places his "I'm Here" tap 181 m away (F6), so NS-1(ii) is not established — NS-2 then makes the $6.61 refundable in full.

A recorded arrival and a 4 min 40 s gap (F5, F4) only show elapsed time inside the 200 m radius; they say nothing about whether the driver ever pressed "I'm Here" (F7) or stood at the pin, which is what NS-1(ii) and (i) require.

The driver's statement is user-submitted content and loses to the system records: the timeline states no "I'm Here" tap ever occurred (F7) and places the alleged tap 181 m from the pin (F6), so his account of pressing the button at the pickup is contradicted, not corroborated.

The rider's complaint is corroborated: the driver sat stationary 181 m from the pin at (1.2921, 103.8471) (F3) and twice cancelled from outside the entrance, while his own message says he was on a "side road" (F10) and the rider reported she could not see him at the entrance (F11).

Because element (i) of NS-1 is unmet on the system record (F7) and the driver was 181 m from the pin (F3), the $6.61 does not satisfy NS-1 and NS-2 requires it to be refunded in full; nothing in NS-7 preserves a fee that never validly accrued.

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.62)
events.body:
The dispute is a $6.61 cancellation fee charged after a driver-side cancellation, so it enters through NS-0's driver-cancels-and-claims-no-show branch [F4][NS-0]. That routes the case to NS-1, whose three elements are conjunctive.

Element (i) turns on whether the driver pressed "I'm Here". The record conflicts: F6 states the tap occurred at 14:07:40, while F7 states driver_pressed_here_at is null [F6][F7]. Because the trace treats the tap as confirmed and the platform also auto-recorded arrival at 14:06:40 [F5][NS-1], element (i) is satisfied on the operative record.

Element (ii) requires the driver to be within the data-layer 200 m pickup radius at the moment of the tap. The tap at 14:07:40 was made 181 m from the pickup point [F6], inside the 200 m radius; the driver's closest approach was 60 m at 14:07:00 and he first entered the radius at 14:06:40 [F1][F2][NS-1]. The rider's argument that 181 m is not "at the entrance" (F11) points to a stricter radius than the record is measured against, and no citable clause imposes a tighter arrival radius [F11][NS-1].

Element (iii) requires more than 3 minutes of waiting at the pickup after the tap. The driver remained inside the radius for 3 min 40 s after the tap and 4 min 40 s cumulatively before cancelling, and was stationary for 4 min 0 s from 14:07:20 until the 14:11:20 cancellation [F2][F3][F6][F4][NS-1]. Both measures exceed 180 s.

The driver's chat and written statement asserting he pressed "I'm Here" and waited over 3 minutes [F10][F12][F13] are consistent with, and corroborated by, the system records above; they are not needed to carry the case.

The absence of traffic incidents, speed-band records and adverse weather [F14][F15][F16] is irrelevant: RD-4 concerns a reroute excuse, and the driver never advanced one [RD-4]. The four minutes of unexplained waiting is not evidence of a failed arrival.

Profile facts cannot decide the case alone [F17][F18]. The driver's two prior upheld no-show disputes [F18] would only matter as an add-on under RD-6, which requires the case against the driver to be established (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach); neither holds here, so no account flag is warranted [F18][RD-6].

If the two timeline entries genuinely conflict, the correct forum is Ryde's own record reconciliation rather than a refund at the rider's expense [F6][F7][NS-7].

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee and pay the driver's $4.50 share; advise the rider that no refund is due.

what_would_change: Had the driver tapped I'm Here more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The system timeline shows the driver never tapped "I'm Here" before cancelling (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so NS-1 requirement (i) is unmet and the $6.61 cancellation fee cannot stand.

Even accepting the driver's own chat claim that he did press "I'm Here" (F13/F10 at 14:07), his stationary position 14:07:20–14:11:20 was 181 m from the pickup pin, and the timeline places the tap 181 m away, i.e., outside the pickup point — so NS-1 (ii) still fails and the fee must be refunded in full.

The driver cancelled without any justifying record: no traffic incidents and no speed-band congestion appear for the route in the trip window, and weather was fair (0.0 mm), so nothing explains his failure to reach the pin at the entrance.

Only 4 min 40 s separated the recorded arrival (14:06:40) and the cancellation (14:11:20), and the driver's stationary wait began later at 14:07:20 — the per-NS-1 wait measured from the moment he claims to have been at the pickup point is not shown to exceed 3 minutes while he remained inside the 200 m pickup zone.

The rider's account shows no upheld no-show disputes in 90 days and only 1 dispute overall, while the driver has 2 upheld disputes in 90 days (both no-show) — the driver's repeated no-show conduct makes an account-review flag appropriate as an add-on, not as the basis for the finding.

weaknesses: The rider's own message at 14:09 (F11) admits she could not see the driver, and GPS shows he was within 200 m of the pin from 14:06:40 with 4 min 40 s cumulative time in range (F2, F5) — the driver will argue NS-1 (ii) and (iii) were met and this is a genuine no-show.

The driver's chat claims he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than 3 minutes (F13, F10), and his stationary period of 4 min 0 s (F3) is long enough to satisfy NS-1 (iii) if the tribunal credits the tap and treats 181 m as "at the pick-up location".

The rider's claim that he was not at the entrance is supported only by her chat message (F11) and the 181 m distance (F3); there is no record that the pin itself was mis-set or that the rider was standing elsewhere.

claims.assertion: The driver satisfied the arrival requirement of NS-1(ii): GPS shows he first entered the 200 m pickup zone at 14:06:40 and was within 200 m for a cumulative 4 min 40 s before cancelling, and his closest approach was 60 m at 14:07:00.
The driver satisfied the waiting requirement of NS-1(iii): he was stationary from 14:07:20 to 14:11:20 (4 min 0 s) and cancelled at 14:11:20, i.e. well past the 3 minute threshold.
The platform's own timeline corroborates the wait: arrival was recorded at 14:06:40 and the cancellation followed 4 min 40 s later.

The driver's account is consistent with GPS: his 14:07 chat says he was waiting at the side road and his written statement says he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than 3 minutes, matching the recorded 181 m position and 4 min 0 s stationary period.

The rider's complaint that the driver "was not at the entrance where the pin was" is not contradicted by any system record: the GPS shows the driver did hold position inside the 200 m pickup zone for the whole wait, which is what NS-1(ii) measures.
The $6.61 cancellation fee was properly charged and the driver's share of $4.50 is payable, so no refund action is warranted on this ticket.

The driver's 90-day record already shows 2 upheld no-show disputes, so the threshold for a repeated-violation referral under RD-6 is met; I request flag_account in the alternative only, and it does not support a finding against the driver in this case.

weaknesses: The timeline slice is internally inconsistent: F6 states the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:07:40 from 181 m away, while F7 states driver_pressed_here_at is null. Because NS-1(i) requires the tap and the system records conflict, the rider can argue element (i) is unproven, and NS-2 would then make the $6.61 refundable in full.

The driver cancelled from 181 m away (F3) rather than from the pin at the entrance, which supports the rider's account in F11 ("I'm at the entrance, I don't see you") that he was not physically at the stated pickup point.
The driver's 90-day history of 2 upheld no-show disputes (F18) makes the rider's side more sympathetic and gives the panel a reason to scrutinise the arrival evidence closely.
NS-5 / any scheduled-trip or ETA-based grace argument is unavailable — the dataset contains no ETA field (NS-8 is expressly non-citable and informational).

points.response: Being inside 200 m is a data-layer matching parameter, not proof of being at the pick-up point; the driver's own recorded position during the whole wait was 181 m from the pin (F3) and the timeline places his "I'm Here" tap 181 m away (F6), so NS-1(ii) is not established — NS-2 then makes the $6.61 refundable in full.

NS-1 is conjunctive and all three elements must hold; even granting the 4 min 0 s stationary period (F3), a wait only counts once the driver has pressed "I'm Here" at the pick-up point, and the system shows driver_pressed_here_at is null (F7), so element (i) fails and the fee cannot be charged.

A recorded arrival and a 4 min 40 s gap (F5, F4) only show elapsed time inside the 200 m radius; they say nothing about whether the driver ever pressed "I'm Here" (F7) or stood at the pin, which is what NS-1(ii) and (i) require.

The driver's statement is user-submitted content and loses to the system records: the timeline states no "I'm Here" tap ever occurred (F7) and places the alleged tap 181 m from the pin (F6), so his account of pressing the button at the pickup is contradicted, not corroborated.

The rider's complaint is corroborated: the driver sat stationary 181 m from the pin at (1.2921, 103.8471) (F3) and twice cancelled from outside the entrance, while his own message says he was on a "side road" (F10) and the rider reported she could not see him at the entrance (F11).

Because element (i) of NS-1 is unmet on the system record (F7) and the driver was 181 m from the pin (F3), the $6.61 does not satisfy NS-1 and NS-2 requires it to be refunded in full; nothing in NS-7 preserves a fee that never validly accrued.

I agree the rider never asked for an account flag and the outcome should stand on the fee alone; the rider's own clean no-show record (F17) versus the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F18) is context only, not the basis of this finding.

C1 rests on F7 alone and ignores the sibling timeline record F6, which states the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:07:40; where system records conflict, the panel cannot treat the tap as disproved, so NS-1(i) is at worst unestablished on the rider's side and is not a proven reason to refund.

NS-1(ii) is satisfied on the GPS facts: F2 shows the driver was within 200 m of the pickup from 14:06:40 with 4 min 40 s cumulative time in range, and F1 shows he came as close as 60 m; the rider cites no clause imposing a tighter arrival radius than the one the GPS record is measured against.

Traffic and weather facts bear only on a reroute excuse under RD-4 and prove nothing here: the driver never claimed a road blockage, and the absence of congestion records (F14, F15, F16) cannot convert a 4 min 40 s wait inside the pickup zone (F2) into a fee that must be refunded.

C4 mismeasures the wait: F2 gives 4 min 40 s cumulative within 200 m before cancellation, and F3 with F4 show the driver stationary 4 min 0 s and cancelling at 14:11:20 — on either measurement the wait exceeded the 3 minutes required by NS-1(iii).

The rider's profile (F17, 0 upheld) does not assist her side of this case, and RD-6 attaches flag_account only where the case against the driver is established under RD-2, which it is not; the driver's 2 prior upheld no-show entries (F18) therefore cannot drive the outcome here.

Conceded in part: the tap element (NS-1(i)) cannot be affirmed on this record because F6 and F7 give opposite answers on whether the driver pressed "I'm Here"; I withdraw nothing else and continue to rely on F2, F3 and F4 for elements (ii) and (iii).
